messages:
cheng li: heads-up — I ran a cross-region + node-topology sweep comparing PCIe-only nodes vs SXM nodes for the new 13B quantized model. Results look weird: peak throughput similar, but 95/99 tail latency on PCIe nodes spikes by ~2.5x when we scale beyond 4 GPUs.
maya r: can you paste the exact numbers? and which regions/hardware variants?
samira: are these with KV-cache warm or cold starts?
cheng li: short summary:
- region eu-west (PCIe A100-40GB) 8-gpu VM: 8 gpus, batch=8, seq=1024 -> throughput 540 tok/s, p95=18ms, p99=124ms
- region us-west (SXM A100-80GB) 8-gpu node: batch=8, seq=1024 -> throughput 560 tok/s, p95=17ms, p99=48ms
- swapping to batch=16 widens gap: pci p99 -> 310ms, sxm p99 -> 62ms
so throughput similar but PCIe tail is terrible.
alex: did you check NVLink topology or NUMA placement? sounds like cross-socket CPU <-> GPU PCIe contention.
cheng li: yes — ran nvidia topo and numactl traces. On the PCIe config some GPUs are on different CPU sockets and have no NVLink between them. nvlink is absent, so all inter-GPU shuffles go over PCIe root complex crossing sockets.
infra-bot: deploy log — benchmark job 1762104321 started by cheng li on infra-bench-06
maya r: any NCCL warnings in the logs? NCCL usually falls back to PCIe for some peerings and that kills latency.
cheng li: NCCL: several warnings about suboptimal bandwidth/peer-to-peer. I grabbed a quick trace:
```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0: GPU1 NV1  GPU2: PCIe(PCIE)  CPU0
GPU1: GPU0 NV1  GPU2: PCIe(PCIE)  CPU0
GPU2: PCIe  GPU3: PCIE  CPU1
```
and process placement was not pinned — containers scheduled by k8s to random cpus.
samira: did you try numactl --cpunodebind or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES ordering?
cheng li: yes. quick experiment:
- unpinned (k8s default): p99 124ms
- numactl --cpunodebind=1 ./serve ... with GPUs local to node1: p99 dropped to 58ms
- setting NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO improved stability
maya r: interesting — so NUMA pinning gave ~2x improvement on PCIe nodes. but SXM still better because of NVLink.
alex: another angle: kernel selection. are we using fused attention kernels on SXM but fallback kernels on PCIe nodes due to different cuBLAS/cuDNN/cuda versions?
cheng li: good call — versions were slightly different across regions (us-west had CUDA 12.2 + cuDNN 9.3, eu-west had CUDA 12.0 + cuDNN 9.1). when I rebuilt runtime with identical stack on PCIe node, p99 improved another ~15%.
maya r: so there are three contributors: NVLink presence (topology), NUMA/cpu-to-gpu pinning, and kernel/runtime mismatches.
samira: did you try using model sharding / KV placement to reduce cross-gpu traffic? for cache-heavy workloads, keeping KV local helps.
cheng li: yes — moving KV cache to local GPU memory and using ring-based all-reduce instead of tree when NVLink unavailable reduced cross-node PCIe transfers and lowered p99 to ~70ms at batch=8.
alex: any configs that we should bake into default deploys? sounds like we need k8s podTopologySpread + nodeSelector for SXM nodes and an init hook that runs numactl pinning.
cheng li: proposal:
- runtime sets CPU pinning based on GPU PCI bus affinity (numactl --cpunodebind)
- runtime checks nvidia-smi topo and selects NCCL algorithm preference (ring vs tree) depending on NVLink connectivity
- demand a minimal CUDA/cuDNN matrix in cloud images and have infra auto-upgrade mismatch nodes
- for Dedicated customers, prefer SXM-backed pools for KV-heavy configs by default
maya r: +1. can you open a tiny RFC with the perf numbers and suggested patches?
samira: also add a quick health-check in console: show NVLink connectivity graph per node and a warning if pods are scheduled across sockets with no NVLink.
cheng li: will do. I'll upload benchmark plots and write the RFC. tagging @alex for infra changes.
alex: thanks — this matches what we've seen on prod incidents where tail latency jumped after scaling to more GPUs on certain instance types. good to have quantitative numbers.
infra-bot: benchmark job 1762104321 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/1762104321/
maya r: awesome. ping when RFC is up and I'll review.
samira: thanks cheng, super actionable. :thumbsup:
